In the rooftop scrape, the raven's body carries heavy momentum into the roof: the bricks and shards have real weight, kicking up and scattering along ballistic arcs with dust before falling, and the hunter's upward jolt and slam-back are driven purely by that impact — no floaty or weightless debris. The 360° is a true roll about the raven's longitudinal axis, one consistent direction, exactly one full rotation back to upright — no random tumbling and no repeated spins. @wire stays taut throughout and clearly visible, its midpoint biting into the raven's neck feathers under load. The hunter's weight loads and unloads violently as he grips, slides, and re-braces; his coat, scarf, and hair whip outward with the roll's centrifugal force. Every position change is driven by visible force — no teleporting between poses.

LIGHTING
Shot 1: warm low sun near the horizon on the facade side of their flight path, visible as a warm glow in the sky. It rim-lights the raven's feathers and the edges of the hunter's coat and hair with warm highlights, while their camera-facing surfaces stay in softer shadow — matching the warm rim-lit look of the reference stills.
Shot 2: they fly straight into the low sun, so the warm sun sits ahead of them and behind the snorricam rig, lighting the hunter's face and front directly — his goggles, scarf, and coat front catch warm golden light, with a soft lens flare/glow. Warm, motivated key from the sun, no artificial fill.

AUDIO
Diegetic only: wind roar, heavy wingbeats, feathers snapping in the turns. The raven shrieks almost continuously across both shots, teeth bared, enraged. The hunter lets out one sharp scream exactly at the inversion peak, and only then; once he is back upright he lets out one audible exhale of relief. No other dialogue. No music or score.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Exactly two figures on the bird throughout: <<<image_2>>> and <<<image_1>>>, no others. The hunter keeps goggles, scarf, and full costume in both shots. @wire remains a single continuous wire with two ends — one gripped in each fist, middle looped tight under and around the raven's throat/neck — and it is clearly visible in every shot, including the wide Shot 1, taut and biting into the neck feathers. The hunter is continuously active and off-balance in Shot 1, never shown calmly seated. The 360° is one single-direction barrel roll about the raven's longitudinal (beak-to-tail) axis, rolling right-to-left (world sweeps right-to-left behind the hunter), that returns exactly to upright — never a random tumble, yaw-spin, or multiple rolls. The roll begins in the final beat of Shot 1 and completes in Shot 2. In Shot 2 the camera is rigidly tied to the hunter's body (true snorricam), never an independent orbiting camera, no rig or mount visible, and they fly straight into the sun so it lights his face. The hunter screams once at full inversion, then exhales in relief once upright. The raven shrieks, glares back at the rider, and tries to throw him off throughout the whole flight. The air and sky stay clear — no floating paper, kite fragments, or drifting debris in either shot. The two shots run as equal halves (~50% / ~50%).

## WORKFLOW METADATA
- User goal: Snowy-mountain blizzard shot. Wide empty valley establisher, HARD CUT to high-angle close-up of a cowboy smoking a pipe who slowly raises his head and gives a threatening/psychopathic smile.

Two-part single clip. First a wide general shot of the frozen valley (so the model locks the full backdrop and does not reuse it as a stuck plate). Then hard cut to a static high-angle (~20 deg down) close-up of the cowboy, head bowed under snow-covered hat, mid slow pipe-drag, who slowly lifts his head to camera, removes the pipe, exhales smoke, and ends on a slow, cold, threatening smile with a killer's eyes.

- <<<48944a64-d64b-4bef-acfa-ba372964b121>>> — location (image 1). Snowy mountain valley, blizzard.
- <<<5ad1aac9-ca55-455f-941c-c5bb00023da5>>> — hero (image 2). Young man, mustache, black wide-brim hat, black cape/coat, dark scarf, red satin tie, white leather gloves.

<<<48944a64-d64b-4bef-acfa-ba372964b121>>> controls valley geometry, treeline placement, mountain/meadow layout, snow materials, overcast diffused atmosphere, cold palette. Controlled two-segment sequence. Exactly ONE hard cut. Real-time, deliberate slow pacing. No other cuts, no montage, no dissolves.

LENS LOCK SEG1 = 84 deg diagonal FOV, classic wide anamorphic landscape character, camera far, epic scale, rectilinear, no fisheye.
LENS LOCK SEG2 = 18 deg diagonal FOV, classic telephoto, tight emotional close-up, compressed snowy bokeh background, subject razor sharp. No drift mid-segment.

SCENE CONTEXT
Two shots separated by ONE hard cut, the whole film playing at constant REAL-TIME 1x speed — no slow motion anywhere. SHOT 1 — PROFILE HIT SHOT: a static, locked, eye-level MEDIUM-WIDE of a golden-hazed ruined Greek acropolis — a huge standing column, a temple colonnade, dusty stone ground, distant fighting far in the haze. THE HERO (the Spartan warrior from the first reference image) stands on the flagstones in the LEFT third of frame, half-turned in profile, crimson cape stirring, his bronze crested helmet on his head, hands empty — no shield, no sword. His face is already tight with dread. He turns to face the RIGHT side of frame — and his eyes go WIDE in raw, Hollywood-caliber TERROR, a gasp, pure horror flashing across his face — as a BURNING ARROW streaks in STRICTLY from the RIGHT part of frame, perfectly horizontal and blindingly fast, and THUDS deep into the center of his chest, its flaming head burying in. The brutal impact hurls him violently BACKWARD off his feet — and knocks his bronze helmet clean OFF his head, the helmet spinning away separately — as he flies flat to the left and OUT of the LEFT edge of frame with the burning arrow embedded upright in his chest; the camera stays locked and never follows. HARD CUT. SHOT 2 — TOP-DOWN DEATH: a static, locked, strict top-down bird's-eye view over the pale dusty flagstones, scattered rubble chips, a long column shadow crossing one corner, golden battle-haze drifting. THE HERO is ALREADY ON THE GROUND as he enters: BARE-HEADED now, his dark curls loose, back grinding along the stone, he shoots in ACROSS the RIGHT edge of frame at ferocious speed, sliding flat on his back in a straight horizontal line, his crimson cape trailing and golden dust pluming behind him, the burning arrow standing rigidly UPRIGHT from his chest toward the camera through the whole slide — and right behind him his bronze crested HELMET skids in across the same RIGHT edge, rolling and scraping along the ground in his wake. He brakes hard to a dead stop in the CENTER of frame — sprawled flat on his back, arms and legs spread, cape settled spread beneath him, face up toward the camera, his face FROZEN in an expression of pure horror, EYES WIDE OPEN in a terrified dead stare straight up into the lens, small flames licking around the embedded arrowhead with thin black smoke curling up — while the helmet rocks to rest on the stone within arm's reach beside him, plainly visible from overhead. There is NO BLOOD anywhere — no red, no bleeding; his only wound is the burning arrow itself. At no point in shot 2 is any part of him airborne: no falling, no landing, no bounce — a pure violent ground slide from the right edge to the center, under one second of real time. The dust settles while the little flame keeps flickering; he never blinks, never breathes, never moves again; the locked camera holds on his death until the clip ends. In shot 2 only this one body, his helmet and the stone are in frame — no archer, no other people, no arrow in flight.

prompt:
SCENE CONTEXT
A chrome flying saucer with four people inside races through a rainy megapolis, fleeing a skyscraper-sized winged monster that smashes through buildings to catch it. The chase ends with the monster's jaws swallowing the camera.

ACTIVE REFERENCES
@vagabond: man around 50, lean weathered war veteran, grey hair, grey-streaked beard, dusty tan t-shirt, bare-metal powered exoskeleton frame strapped on his arms and shoulders. He pilots the saucer, hands wrestling the right-side steering wheel. 100% matches the reference.
@spyke: young man, wild fluffy black hair, thin mustache, dark green suit jacket with sleeves pushed up over a rust-orange shirt, loose dark tie. 100% matches the reference.
@mia: young woman, shaggy ash-silver hair with messy fringe, small silver septum ring, cropped burgundy leather jacket over a black crop top. 100% matches the reference.
@chung: young man with a shaved head, blue-grey right eye, scar through his right eyebrow, black dragon tattoo running down the right side of his face and neck, rust-orange suede bomber jacket over a white tee, thin silver chain. 100% matches the reference.
@ship: retro 1950s chrome-silver flying saucer, wide flat disc body, fully transparent glass bubble dome, four grey leather seats in two rows, steering wheel on the right side, thin antenna on top. 100% matches the reference.
@monster: colossal winged demon the size of a city block — single glowing red eye in a horned rocky head, spiked writhing tentacle-horns, cracked black stone-armor plates over pale sinewy limbs, huge tattered bat wings, four legs with long black claws, fanged jaws. 100% matches the reference. Scale lock: it towers over multi-story buildings; its wingspan spans the whole street canyon.
@location: modern megapolis center in gloomy overcast weather — deep street canyon of glass and stone towers, low storm clouds swallowing the tallest rooftops, light steady rain, wet reflective asphalt, scattered yellow taxis and umbrellas far below. Reference controls geography, architecture, palette and weather only.

FORMAT MODE
CONTROLLED MULTI-SHOT SEQUENCE, six segments, five HARD CUTs. Real-time motion inside each segment. No other cuts, no dissolves, no speed ramps.

SHOT 1 — 0.0s to 1.0s
First frame: @ship already in frame close to camera, upper-left, nose tilted down. It dives past the camera between two towers, engine wailing, rain streaking off its chrome hull, and drops toward the street canyon below. The ship's speed is fast relative to the near camera and the nearby asteroids, so it shrinks quickly in perspective; but the station is kilometers away, so even at high speed the ship closes only a negligible fraction of that distance during the shot and never arrives. A still, bright, hazy winter afternoon high over an old stone city, the sun buried in the haze and never visible, a thin layer of snow lying on every roof and ledge. A giant mutant raven with a man riding its shoulders bursts backward through the stone wheel window high on a pale limestone gothic cathedral wall, and the two fight in open air: the raven beats to climb and tries to throw him off, the hunter hauls a silver wire around its neck to force its head down and drive it to the ground.

The reference controls architecture, tracery structure, stone material and color, city layout, street position, altitude, atmosphere and light quality. The camera vantage is set by the CAMERA section of this prompt, not by the reference framing.
<<<image_2>>> — enormous mutant raven, glossy shaggy wet-looking black plumage, bare dark wrinkled skin over the skull, long reptilian beak lined with jagged teeth and pale bone-grey at the tip, pale milky eyes, thick scaled clawed legs. Scale lock, held in every segment: body 7 m from beak tip to tail tip, 5.5 m tall standing, wingspan 14 m. Read that scale through direct comparison with the man on its back, not through absolute size — his whole standing body is about one seventh of the wingspan and a little over a quarter of the body length; one wing from shoulder to tip is roughly three and a half times his height; the head and beak together are about as long as he is tall; its eye is the size of his fist; one rear claw is as long as his forearm; the longest primary feathers are each about the length of his whole arm. Standing on its shoulders he occupies only the middle quarter of the width of its back, between the wing roots, and his silhouette rises above the spine by only about a quarter of the body length. The wingspan is a little wider than the wheel window it has just broken through, and wider than the snow-covered street far below; compared to the city underneath, it spans the full ridge of a single townhouse roof, while the man on its back is no taller than one of the crocketed pinnacles on the buttresses beside him. Action-critical: a thin silver wire is wrapped once around its neck and bites into the neck feathers. 100% matches the reference.
<<<image_3>>> — adult male, about 190 cm, long dark wavy hair, mustache and light stubble, a small pale scar through the right eyebrow, round dark-lens goggles over the eyes, lower face bare and fully visible with no scarf and no face covering. Worn dark teal-blue leather longcoat, tan brocade waistcoat, dark turtleneck, layered worn-leather bracers and gloves, tall brown boots, sword sheathed in the back harness and never drawn. Action-critical: both gloved hands grip the taut silver wire and haul it backward and down, boots planted on the raven's shoulder blades. Face and costume 100% match the reference, except the burgundy scarf is removed.

LOCATION MAP
Exterior, open air outside the cathedral facade, about 60 m above a snow-covered city street. The camera floats in open air about 22 m out from the facade plane and about 14 m above the center of the wheel window, tilted down about 25°. From there the pale limestone facade carrying the wheel window stands obliquely across screen-left and its lower tiers drop away toward the bottom-left corner; the flank of the building steps away from the window into depth toward center-right as a receding file of buttresses, each capped with a tall crocketed pinnacle and each carrying a carved gargoyle waterspout thrown out over the void; one tall thin dark spire rises behind that file. Open pale sky fills the upper right, and below and beyond it the dark old city spreads across the whole right side of frame, far down and far away: steep slate and half-timbered gable roofs packed shoulder to shoulder, dense rows of chimneys, and a snow-covered paved street running diagonally down through them, with a distant skyline of spires and towers bleached almost to nothing in bright haze along the far edge. Every tracery cell is filled with thin leaded panels of near-black glass that carry no color and no light of their own, so the wheel reads as a pale stone lattice over a black void. Behind the glazing the cathedral interior is a black void. Straight lines stay rectilinear, no fisheye curve, no circular vignette. As the raven drives out toward the lens its wings expand to fill the frame edge to edge without the lens changing.
Segment 2: 47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character, camera 18 to 22 m from the pair — far enough that the full 14 m wingspan sits inside frame with natural body proportions and no compression, pale facade and dark city both readable behind them.
Segments 3 and 4: 29° diagonal field of view, short telephoto portrait character, camera 4 to 6 m from the subject, tight framing achieved through lens reach, subject razor-sharp, background compressed into a soft wash.
Segment 5: 18° diagonal field of view, classic telephoto lens character, camera 120 to 160 m above and behind the pair along their fall line, looking down. 1.2s to 1.4s — A muffled impact behind the glass, dust jets out of the stone joints, one glass panel cracks.
1.4s to 2.2s — Real time. The raven's back and the hunter's shoulders smash out through the glazing; leaded panels blow outward, several tracery bars snap, the central boss breaks free, grey dust blasts out. All the snow held on the tracery and the window ring is thrown off at once as a low ring of powder that drifts far slower than the glass. The wings snap open and grab air, and the downwash strips the loose top layer of snow off the balustrade and the gallery roof below in a low sheet. The hunter's knees absorb the jolt and both fists stay locked on the wire.
2.2s — SPEED RAMP into slow motion.
2.2s to 3.4s — Slow motion. The pair sink away from the facade. The raven twists its neck and shrieks; the hunter leans back with both arms straight, hauling the wire down and to the right.
3.4s HARD CUT
3.4s to 6.0s — Segment 2, slow motion, medium. Both are clear of the facade, out over the void with the dark city below them. The raven throws two heavy asymmetric downstrokes to climb and rolls hard onto its left side to spill him off; the hunter's boots slide across the wet feathers, he drops to one knee, jams a shoulder against the wing root and keeps both fists closed on the wire. He hauls down and to the right like a rein; the beak is dragged down and the whole body pitches nose-down. The raven answers with a rear claw raking up along its own flank at his leg and its head snapping back over its shoulder, teeth closing on air a hand's width from his arm. Glass and stone still drift around them.
6.0s HARD CUT
6.0s to 7.6s — Segment 3, slow motion, close-up on <<<image_3>>>. Jaw clenched, teeth bared, lips pulled back, cords standing out in his neck, brow tight, cheek muscle trembling with effort, breath forced out through the teeth. Hair and coat collar whip in the airflow. Both fists shake on the wire and the line cuts into the leather of his gloves. Glass dust and grit sit on his shoulders and blow off in the wind. Two small pale sky reflections sit in the goggle lenses.
7.6s HARD CUT
7.6s to 9.2s — Segment 4, slow motion, close-up on <<<image_2>>>'s head. The toothed beak gapes wide in a scream, the long tongue unfurls and vibrates, strings of spit stretch and break, breath fogs the cold air. The silver wire is buried in the compressed neck feathers with the skin dented under it. The pale milky eye rolls back and locks onto the hunter.
9.2s HARD CUT
9.2s to 10.2s — Segment 5, slow motion, high angle from above. They have lost most of their height and are now only 40 to 60 m above the city, so the snow-covered roofscape fills the entire frame with no sky and no horizon. Out-of-focus glass shards tumble and spin close to the lens as large soft dark shapes at the frame edges, sharp first; the two struggling figures are small, soft and near frame center below, x≈48%, y≈45%, black against the pale snowy roofs and the dark slate showing through them.
10.2s — Focus racks off the foreground shards back onto the pair, and as focus lands the motion SPEED RAMPS back to real time.
10.2s to 12.0s — Real time. The raven's head is hauled fully down, the climb collapses, the wings hammer out of rhythm, and the pair drop fast toward the snow-covered roofs directly below, glass and stone falling ahead of them and punching dark holes through the white as they land ahead of the pair. The camera holds the high angle and follows them down.

PHYSICS
The window fails as stone and old glass, not as a single sheet. The thin leaded panels go first: each tracery cell blows outward as a fan of small irregular shards, the lead strips tearing and curling like wire ribbon and staying half-attached to the stone edges. Then the slender tracery bars snap at their thinnest necks into short carved stone batons, and the round central boss cracks free as one heavy chunk. The heavy outer ring and the surround hold, leaving a ragged hole through the lower right of the wheel with broken bars pointing inward. Old glass breaks small and dusty, in irregular fragments and glass powder rather than large clean plates. Grey mortar dust and centuries of interior grime blast out with the pressure and hang in the air behind the pair. The stone resists: the raven's backward momentum visibly checks for a fraction of a beat at contact before it breaks through, and the recoil travels through its body into the hunter's braced knees. Debris then separates by weight — stone fragments fall fast and almost straight and punch clean-edged holes through the thin snow on the balustrade rails and the ledges below the window, skidding and scarring dark lines through the white, while glass falls slower, fluttering and spinning, catching cold pale light and shrinking away toward the street tens of meters down. The snow behaves as dry, cold, lightly packed powder: struck or blown, it puffs and drifts as a low slow cloud rather than splashing or smearing, it keeps a crisp rim where anything presses into it, and airborne powder falls far slower than glass or stone, drifting sideways on the wind and still hanging in the air long after the heavy debris has gone. On the gallery roof one loosened slab shears along a straight break line, slides accelerating over the slick tiles, drops off the eave and bursts into powder in mid-fall. Snow that lands on the hunter's shoulders and on the raven's wet feathers darkens and melts into droplets, while snow on cold stone and cold leather stays dry and brushes off as powder. The wings move air with real mass: feather tips bend under load, the body rises on each downstroke, and the whole animal is heavy and slow to turn. The rider's full weight sits on the shoulders — boots press into the plumage and slip on the wet feathers, the longcoat drags and cracks in the airflow, hair lags behind every head movement, and the sheathed sword swings and knocks against the back harness. The wire stays thin and taut, compressing the neck under it while the raven's breath saws and its head fights the pull. In slow motion glass, feathers, dust and cloth each keep their own inertia; when speed snaps back everything accelerates with weight. Flight motion is continuous throughout, with no floating and no jumping between poses.

LIGHTING
One natural source only: a high sun buried in thick bright winter haze, off frame beyond the upper left, its disc never visible. Exposure is set for the pale limestone and its snow, not for the sky and not for the city. The light is soft and directional at once — it comes from high and from camera-left, so it lands on the facade plane and on the left-facing flanks of the buttresses and pinnacles, and those planes are the brightest architecture in frame, a cool pale ivory-grey stone with only the faintest sandy warmth left in it. Shadow edges stay soft-ish because the haze diffuses everything — no hard black-edged cast shadows, no long raking shadows, no sun disc, no lens flare, no golden or orange cast anywhere in frame. The sky is a cool pale blue-grey, faintly deeper at the very top of frame and washing out to near-white where it meets the haze at the horizon; it is bright but it is not the brightest thing in the shot, because the lit limestone and the snow sit above it. Depth runs bright, then dark, then bright: near limestone bright and high in contrast, the mid-distance city a dark brown-black mass of slate, timber and shadowed streets with its contrast already falling, and the far skyline bleached by haze until the snow-covered roofs and the sky lose separation almost completely and only distant spire tips punctuate it. Out in the open air the pair are keyed from above and from camera-left, so the light wraps: broad soft pale speculars run along the wet black feathers and over the crest of the raven's back, thin wing membranes glow faintly where the light passes through, and the hunter's brow, cheekbones and knuckles catch soft cool light while his eye sockets and lower jaw fall into gentle shade. Shadow edges stay soft and his expression stays readable in every close-up; no hard shadow lines on the face. The goggle lenses hold two small pale sky catchlights. The two figures read differently against each background and that reversal is deliberate: against the bright limestone and against the sky they darken toward silhouette with a bright rim along their contours, and against the dark city below them they read the other way, pale-rimmed and separated by those wet speculars. Behind the breach the interior stays a black void, with only a thin wash of daylight now reaching a couple of meters inside to show bare stone and swirling dust at the edge of the fresh hole while the depth beyond stays black. The palette is cool and desaturated, close to monochrome: pale ivory-grey limestone, near-white snow, slate blue-grey shadow, grey-blue haze, and the dark brown-black city, with no warm bounce light anywhere in the environment. The snow is the brightest thing in frame and sits just above the lit stone in exposure — near-white but never clipping, matte and fine-grained with no sparkle at all, because sparkle needs direct sun and there is none; it holds a faint cool blue-grey in every dent, drift shadow, footprint and crease. Because it lies only on upward faces, the city reads as pale horizontal planes stacked between dark vertical walls, and every ledge, cornice, rail, pinnacle tip and gargoyle back on the facade is drawn with a brighter line. The snow throws a weak, soft, cool fill upward, faintly lifting the soffits under the eaves, the undersides of the gargoyles and the belly and wing undersides of the raven whenever it passes low over a roof, but the hazy sun above stays the dominant key and this bounce never becomes a second light. Natural daylight only, no artificial fill, no lamps, no sunset color.

AUDIO
Diegetic sound only. The first 1.2 s is calm and acoustically deadened by the snow: faint high wind and a thin distant murmur rising from the street far below, muffled and softened, with no reverberation off the rooftops. Then a muffled boom behind the glass, then the break — bright shattering leaded glass, dry cracking stone, and fragments landing on the snow-covered balustrades and ledges below as dull soft thuds rather than bright clatter, with the hiss of a snow slab sliding and dropping away. Then the raven's guttural ear-splitting shriek, heavy wingbeats thumping displaced air, rushing wind, leather and cloth snapping, the thin creak of the taut wire, the animal's sawing breath, and the man's hard breathing and wordless effort grunts through his teeth. The audio stretches and drops in pitch through the slow-motion segments and snaps back to full speed with the picture in segment five. No spoken words, no dialogue, no narration, no music, no subtitles.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
The only two living figures that read anywhere in frame are <<<image_2>>> and <<<image_3>>>. No other birds and no other animals. Any distant traffic on the street far below stays unresolvable dark texture and never becomes a recognizable person, and no person appears at the cathedral level.
The hunter keeps the goggles on, his lower face bare, and both gloved hands on the silver wire in every segment; the sword stays sheathed on his back.
The silver wire stays wrapped once around the raven's neck and stays taut in every segment.
The raven stays enormous beside the 190 cm man in every segment, including in wide and high-angle framings where both are small in frame: his standing body stays about one seventh of the wingspan, the head and beak stay about as long as he is tall, and he stays a small load riding the middle quarter of the width of its back. He never grows to look like half the length of its body, and the wings never shorten to look like a large eagle's.
Their opposed intentions stay visible in the action: the raven fights to climb and to throw him off, the hunter fights to force its head down and drive it toward the ground.
Bright hazy daytime with a high hidden sun is the lighting condition in every segment: the lit pale limestone and the snow stay the brightest things in frame, the sky stays a cool pale blue-grey below them in exposure, the mid-distance city stays a dark band and the far skyline stays bleached by haze, and the cathedral interior behind the breach stays black.
Snow quantity stays locked in every segment at a thin 2 to 4 cm layer on upward-facing surfaces only, with all vertical faces and undersides bare, tile courses and carving still reading through the snow, and no deep drifts, no smooth white blanket and no falling snowfall in the air.

The first frame is intentionally free of figures for 1.2 s to hold the calm of the city before the break, then the action begins. Frame one: the intact wheel window sits screen-right, x=52–88%, y=8–66%, its dark glazing unbroken, the whole wheel inside frame. Shadowed near-black stone wall, pier and carving span x=44–100%. The snow-capped quatrefoil balustrade and its gargoyles run across x=48–100%, y=62–90%. The nave roof, stair turret and pinnacle file occupy x=34–52%, y=24–78%. Blown-out hazy sky fills x=0–40% over the upper two thirds. The distant city band sits in deep background, x=0–34%, y=72–100%, its snow-covered roof planes reading as pale flats against black walls, with the single tall dark spire at x≈12%, y=74–92%. Snow traces the whole architecture in frame: rounded pale caps along the balustrade rail at y=64–70%, pale crescents on the upward faces of the window tracery, and an unbroken white plane on the nave roof at center-left. Real time for the calm and the break, one speed ramp into slow motion at 2.2 s, sustained slow motion through segments two, three and four, one speed ramp back to real time inside segment five. Continuity across every segment: same hazy winter daylight, same locked snow layer, raven enormous, hunter on its shoulders with both gloved hands on the taut wire, wire wrapped once around the neck, bare face with goggles, glass and stone dust still hanging in the air. Altitude falls steadily from segment to segment as they lose height, ending low over the rooftops. The camera stays on the same side of the action throughout, with no axis crossing.

Segment 1: 47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character, camera 34 to 38 m out from the wall plane, natural human-eye perspective, no distortion, the whole wheel window, the balustrade below it and the distant city band all inside frame. As the raven drives out toward the lens its wings fill the frame edge to edge without the lens changing.
Segment 2: 47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character, camera 18 to 22 m from the pair — far enough that the full 14 m wingspan sits inside frame with natural body proportions and no compression, black stone and pale distant city both readable behind them.
Segments 3 and 4: 29° diagonal field of view, short telephoto portrait character, camera 4 to 6 m from the subject, tight framing achieved through lens reach, subject razor-sharp, background compressed into a soft pale wash.
Segment 5: 18° diagonal field of view, classic telephoto lens character, camera 120 to 160 m above and behind the pair along their fall line, looking down. CAMERA
An airborne operator in open air, always outside the wall and always to the left of the window, never crossing to the other side of the action. Segment 1: locked off and completely still through the calm 1.2 s, then one hard handheld jolt on the impact with real shoulder-mounted mass, a single flinch and a human re-frame rather than digital shake, then settling into a slow drift as the pair fall away from the wall. Segment 2: the camera flies with them, matching their fall, holding them at frame center-left while the black stone slides through the right of frame to prove speed and altitude. Segments 3 and 4: tight slow float with slight operator breathing weight, subject held steady in frame. Segment 5: a high angle from well above and behind-left of the pair, still on the same side of the action and never crossing it, tilted down about 50° so the snowy roofscape fills the whole frame and the two figures sit small near frame center against it. The camera drifts slowly down and forward with them, holding them centered as they lose the last of their height, then stays with them as the speed snaps back and they drop toward the roofs.

ACTION TIMING
0.0s to 1.2s — Calm. Still frame, quiet city, intact window, hazy daylight, nothing moving but haze.
1.2s to 1.4s — A muffled impact behind the glass, dust jets out of the stone joints, one glass panel cracks.
1.4s to 2.2s — Real time. The raven's back and the hunter's shoulders smash out through the glazing; leaded panels blow outward, several tracery bars snap, the central boss breaks free, grey dust blasts out. All the snow held on the tracery and the window ring is thrown off at once as a low ring of powder that drifts far slower than the glass. 6.0s HARD CUT

Jaw clenched, teeth bared, lips pulled back, cords standing out in his neck, brow tight, cheek muscle trembling with effort, breath forced out through the teeth. Hair and coat collar whip in the airflow. Both fists shake on the wire and the line cuts into the leather of his gloves. Glass dust and grit sit on his shoulders and blow off in the wind. Two small pale sky reflections sit in the goggle lenses.
7.6s HARD CUT
7.6s to 9.2s — Segment 4, slow motion, close-up on <<<image_2>>>'s head. The toothed beak gapes wide in a scream, the long tongue unfurls and vibrates, strings of spit stretch and break, breath fogs the cold air. 10.2s to 12.0s — Real time. The raven's head is hauled fully down, the climb collapses, the wings hammer out of rhythm, and the pair drop fast toward the snow-covered roofs directly below, glass and stone falling ahead of them and punching dark holes through the white as they land ahead of the pair. The camera holds the high angle and follows them down.

PHYSICS
The window fails as stone and old glass, not as a single sheet. The thin leaded panels go first: each tracery cell blows outward as a fan of small irregular shards, the lead strips tearing and curling like wire ribbon and staying half-attached to the stone edges. Then the slender tracery bars snap at their thinnest necks into short carved stone batons, and the round central boss cracks free as one heavy chunk. The heavy outer ring and the square surround hold, leaving a ragged hole through the lower left of the wheel with broken bars pointing inward. Old glass breaks small and dusty, in irregular fragments and glass powder rather than large clean plates. Grey mortar dust and centuries of interior grime blast out with the pressure and hang in the air behind the pair. The stone resists: the raven's backward momentum visibly checks for a fraction of a beat at contact before it breaks through, and the recoil travels through its body into the hunter's braced knees. Debris then separates by weight — stone fragments fall fast and almost straight and punch clean-edged holes through the thin snow on the balustrade rail and the nave roof below the window, skidding and scarring dark slate lines through the white, while glass falls slower, fluttering and spinning, catching cold pale light and shrinking away toward the rooftops hundreds of meters down. The snow behaves as dry, cold, lightly packed powder: struck or blown, it puffs and drifts as a low slow cloud rather than splashing or smearing, it keeps a crisp rim where anything presses into it, and airborne powder falls far slower than glass or stone, drifting sideways on the wind and still hanging in the air long after the heavy debris has gone. On the nave roof one loosened slab shears along a straight break line, slides accelerating over the slick tiles, drops off the eave and bursts into powder in mid-fall. Snow that lands on the hunter's shoulders and on the raven's wet feathers darkens and melts into droplets, while snow on cold stone and cold leather stays dry and brushes off as powder. The wings move air with real mass: feather tips bend under load, the body rises on each downstroke, and the whole animal is heavy and slow to turn. The rider's full weight sits on the shoulders — boots press into the plumage and slip on the wet feathers, the longcoat drags and cracks in the airflow, hair lags behind every head movement, and the sheathed sword swings and knocks against the back harness. The wire stays thin and taut, compressing the neck under it while the raven's breath saws and its head fights the pull. In slow motion glass, feathers, dust and cloth each keep their own inertia; when speed snaps back everything accelerates with weight. Flight motion is continuous throughout, with no floating and no jumping between poses.

LIGHTING
One natural source only: a bright hazy sky, with the sun hidden high behind thin haze and outside the frame on the far side of the wall. Exposure is set for the pale blown-out ivory sky, not for the stone and not for the faces. The sun sits high, well above the horizon, and is never seen: no sun disc, no horizon glow, no long raking shadows, no golden or orange cast anywhere in frame. The sky is an almost even blown-out white dome, only marginally cooler and faintly blue-grey toward the upper left, with no gradient running down to the horizon. Nothing in the city and nothing on the building catches a direct beam — every plane turned toward camera sits in shade, and the sky itself is the only bright thing in the shot. The cathedral wall faces away from the sun, so all its stone stays crushed near-black and reads almost as silhouette, with only cool pale skylight grazing the top edges of the cornices, the balustrade rail, the pinnacles, the gargoyle backs and the carving. Out in the open air the pair are keyed from straight above by the huge soft sky, so the light wraps: broad soft pale speculars run along the wet black feathers and over the crest of the raven's back, thin wing membranes glow faintly where the light passes through, and the hunter's brow, cheekbones and knuckles catch soft cool light while his eye sockets and lower jaw fall into gentle shade. Shadow edges stay soft and his expression stays readable in every close-up; no hard shadow lines and no warm tone anywhere in frame. The goggle lenses hold two small pale sky catchlights. Against the pale sky both figures darken toward silhouette with a bright rim along their contours; against the black stone they separate through those cool speculars. Behind the breach the interior stays a black void, with only a thin wash of daylight now reaching a couple of meters inside to show bare stone and swirling dust at the edge of the fresh hole while the depth beyond stays black. The palette is cool, neutral and desaturated, very close to monochrome, with a faint blue-teal cast in the stone: black stone, pale ivory sky, grey-blue haze, white roof planes, dark slate showing through thin snow, and no warm bounce light anywhere in the environment. The snow is the second brightest thing in frame after the sky and sits just under it in exposure — near-white but never clipping, matte and fine-grained with no sparkle at all, because sparkle needs direct sun and there is none; it holds a faint cool blue-grey in every dent, drift shadow and crease. Because it lies only on upward faces, the whole city reads as pale horizontal planes stacked between black vertical walls, and the black cathedral wall is drawn with thin pale lines wherever a ledge, cornice, rail or cusp catches it. The snow throws a weak, soft, cool fill upward, faintly lifting the soffits under the eaves, the underside of the balustrade and the belly and wing undersides of the raven whenever it passes low over a roof, but the sky dome above stays the dominant key and this bounce never becomes a second light. Thick bright haze fills the distance, so contrast falls off steadily with depth and the far city ends up paler than everything near the camera; at the horizon the snow-covered roofs and the pale sky lose separation almost completely, and only the one dark spire and the chimney stacks punctuate the haze. Natural daylight only, no artificial fill, no lamps, no sunset color.

AUDIO
Diegetic sound only. The first 1.2 s is calm and acoustically deadened by the snow: faint high wind and a distant city murmur muffled and softened, with no reverberation off the rooftops. Then a muffled boom behind the glass, then the break — bright shattering leaded glass, dry cracking stone, and fragments landing on the snow-covered balustrade and nave roof below as dull soft thuds rather than bright clatter, with the hiss of a snow slab sliding and dropping away. Then the raven's guttural ear-splitting shriek, heavy wingbeats thumping displaced air, rushing wind, leather and cloth snapping, the thin creak of the taut wire, the animal's sawing breath, and the man's hard breathing and wordless effort grunts through his teeth. The audio stretches and drops in pitch through the slow-motion segments and snaps back to full speed with the picture in segment five. No spoken words, no dialogue, no narration, no music, no subtitles.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Exactly two living figures appear in the whole sequence: <<<image_2>>> and <<<image_3>>>. No other people and no other birds or animals.
The hunter keeps the goggles on, his lower face bare, and both gloved hands on the silver wire in every segment; the sword stays sheathed on his back.
The silver wire stays wrapped once around the raven's neck and stays taut in every segment.
The raven stays enormous beside the 190 cm man in every segment, including in wide and high-angle framings where both are small in frame: his standing body stays about one seventh of the wingspan, the head and beak stay about as long as he is tall, and he stays a small load riding the middle quarter of the width of its back. He never grows to look like half the length of its body, and the wings never shorten to look like a large eagle's.
Their opposed intentions stay visible in the action: the raven fights to climb and to throw him off, the hunter fights to force its head down and drive it toward the ground.
Bright hazy daytime with a high hidden sun is the lighting condition in every segment: the sky is the only light source and the only bright thing in frame, the near stone stays the darkest thing in frame while the distant city stays paler than it, and the cathedral interior behind the breach stays black.
Snow quantity stays locked in every segment at a thin 3 to 6 cm layer on upward-facing surfaces only, with all vertical faces and undersides bare, tile courses and carving still reading through the snow, and no deep drifts, no smooth white blanket and no falling snowfall in the air.

SCENE CONTEXT

A hunter has cornered a giant mutant raven inside the stone tower of a gothic cathedral. The fight is already lost control of: he has thrown a heavy silver chain around the bird's neck, hauled himself onto its back and is trying to ride it down and choke it out. The raven is not tamed and not carrying him — it is fighting for its life, bucking, hammering its wings against the tower walls and clawing at the chain to get it off its throat and to throw the man off its spine. Neither of them intends to leave the tower. Mid-struggle the raven's back slams into the great rose window and the two of them are thrown out into open air by accident, still fighting. We pick up at the instant of the impact and follow the chaotic airborne struggle in slow motion, ending as time snaps back to full speed.

ACTIVE REFERENCES

<<<image_1>>> (ref image 1) — THE HUNTER: adult male, ~190 cm, long dark wavy hair, round dark-lens goggles over the eyes, deep burgundy cloth scarf covering the lower half of his face from nose to neck, worn dark teal-blue leather longcoat, tan brocade waistcoat, dark turtleneck, layered worn-leather bracers and fingerless leather gloves, tall worn brown riding boots. Action-critical: both gloved hands are wrapped around a taut heavy silver chain and haul it backward with his whole body weight; his boots fight for grip on the raven's back and keep slipping. Use the costume from this reference only. 100% matches reference image 1.

<<<image_3>>> (ref image 3) — THE RAVEN: enormous mutant raven, oily shaggy black plumage in ragged clumps, elongated reptilian beak lined with uneven jagged teeth, bare scarred grey-black skin around the face, pale milky blind-looking eyes, thick heavily scaled clawed legs, hooked claws. The falling hunter's coat, his BARE FACE and the blade are lit from the upper left with hard shadow on the opposite side; his face is modelled by that light and stays fully legible with real skin texture, never crushed to a black shape, never blown out by the flare and never flatly front-lit — bounce off the sunlit stone below opens up its shadow side just enough to hold the features. Exposure is set for the two figures, not the sky, so his face, the closing gap and the moment the blade passes under the bird all stay legible. No flat frontal fill anywhere.
Overall high-contrast — bright sunlit stone against warm open shadow. Filmic, naturally exposed cinematic image with photographic contrast — the look of a live-action film shot on a clear sunny afternoon.

Airflow at flight speed drives everything: his hair streams straight back, his coat tails and collar flap and slap, the loose corners of the sheet snap and crack. Loud rushing wind at high flight speed, rising and falling with each bank, heavy powerful wingbeats and feather rustle, harsh guttural cries from the raven as it fights the chain, hard clinking and snatching of steel chain links, a sharp cloth snap and crack as the sheet is ripped off and flung away, its flutter falling off fast behind him as it recedes, faint city ambience far below. From him: strained breathing, a loud hard exhale of relief around 4.5s, a sharp sudden intake of breath through the nose at 5.6s cut off as his mouth clamps shut, and held, tight, shallow breathing through the nose from 6.3s to the end. They are thrown away by his hand, not merely blown off, they never come back, and they are never dropped out of frame instantly.
The face reveal is permanent: from 2.4s onward his face is completely uncovered, with no goggles, no bandana and no cloth returning to his face.
Hand states are exact: 0.0-0.7s one chain run in each fist, 0.7-8.0s both runs clamped in the left fist alone, 1.6-2.9s the sheet bundle in the right hand until he flings it away at 2.9s, 2.9-8.0s the right hand empty.
There is no braking action anywhere in the shot: he never hauls back on the chains, never pulls the reins, never yanks the bird's head back, and the raven never slows, never pitches nose-high and never breaks into a braking wingbeat. The flight speed and rhythm stay the same from the first frame to the last, and the shot ends on fear alone.
The seat and the chain rig hold for the whole shot exactly as in @ref: he stays astride at the base of the neck with knees raised and boots braced on the bird's shoulders, and the chain stays looped around the base of the beak with its two runs crossing his body to his gloved fists. He never stands, never dismounts and never loses the chain.
The rider stays fixed in frame the whole time and the world moves around him, as the camera is bolted to his body.
The flight is fast, hard and unstable from the first frame to the last: the raven is always banking, rolling, yawing or fighting the chain, and the background never sits level or steady.
His head stays up and his face stays aimed forward along the flight path, straight at the camera, for all eight seconds. His chin stays level or lifted, never tucked. He looks ahead of himself at all times and never looks down at his hands, at the chain, at the bird under him or at the rooftops below, and never turns to look back at the thrown bundle. Only his eyelids and expression change during the blinking beat, not the direction his head points.
Emotion is played at full blockbuster scale and reads clearly on the face at all times: strained effort, then a wide open grin of relief, then, in a single frame, huge wide-eyed terror with the face tense and the mouth clamped tightly shut. From 5.5s onward his mouth stays closed and his eyes stay wide and fixed forward.
The action runs as one unbroken take with no cuts, no dissolves, no speed ramps and no camera moves independent of the rider's body.
Everything ahead of him, including the wall he reacts to, remains outside the frame and is never revealed.
Kodak Vision3 250D daylight, real film grain, grounded physical cinema texture, high-budget practical-effects look.

PHYSICS
The raven has mass. Every downbeat drives the body up and forward and the rider's weight lands into the saddle a fraction late; every upstroke lets the body sink and the rider goes light. That two-beat rise and fall runs through the whole frame.
The neck is a real neck: extended in cruise so the beak sits low and far, retracted into the dive so the head pulls back toward the rider and the beak wedge grows in frame, and shaken as a heavy weighted mass that swings past its stopping point and settles.
The chains are heavy steel. Slack chain hangs in a real catenary and swings a beat behind the bird; tensioned chain is a rigid line that transmits the jerk instantly to the harness ring. Links rattle and grind, and when the right chain lets go it travels as a whipping wave along its length.
Leather resists: gauntlets crease across the knuckles under load, buckled straps pull tight and wrist edges dig in, and the chain drags across the palm leather with friction before it slips.
Air has force at this speed: hair whipping chaotically across the top and side edges of frame, coat sleeves hammering, loose black feathers tearing free during the dive and tumbling past the camera on the airflow rather than straight back, the bird's whole airframe trembling.
Perspective and blur obey distance: a chimney two meters off the wingtip crosses the whole frame in three or four frames as a hard directional streak, mid-distance roofs slide steadily, and the hazed towers on the horizon barely move. The target grows on an accelerating curve rather than at a constant rate.
The roll is a real banked turn: the bird drops a shoulder, the horizon tilts, and the rider's body and camera follow a beat late and overshoot slightly on the recovery.
The dive is a real aerodynamic event: the bird gains speed as it loses height and the tuck cuts drag, then the wings cup open and it dumps that speed in a hard flare — and it is that deceleration, not a shove, that throws the rider's mass forward and breaks his right-hand grip.
Everything in frame has weight, and every change of state has a visible cause one beat earlier.

Materials completely real: skin, cloth, feathers, forged steel, slate, plaster, brick, glass, dust. The roof being flat is why friction and not slope governs his footing — driving strides on smooth dusty level slate with poor grip, slates shifting and dust bursting under each footfall, and the push-off is one loaded stride into a ballistic arc. The draw is one practiced motion without breaking stride, the freed straps snapping back against his coat and then flapping loose. The window shatters as a slow expanding sheet; the wings open with the real inertia of a five-to-six-metre span. The bird is already at full flight speed as it leaves the wall and simply sustains it — not a dodge, not an acceleration. The sword has real weight in the one hand that keeps it: it hangs and swings from his wrist under its own mass rather than being held aimed, and the copper gear at its base carries that same weight with it.

Destruction. The leaded light fails at the lead, not the glass: the H-section cames tear and peel back like ribbon, staying attached at the sill, while the crown glass leaves in thick curved shards 5 to 15 cm across with greenish edges and visible ripple — irregular shards, never small cubes. The oak mullion and frame are riven oak: they split along the grain into long splinters and shear at the pegs rather than shattering. The lime-plaster infill blows out in flat plate-shaped chunks 20 to 60 cm wide, white-faced with a straw-flecked brown daub core, and the riven laths behind them spring and snap. The 12 cm oak studs break green-wood: they hinge, splinter and stay attached. Every piece leaves the hole inside a cone centred on <<<7ac036f0-ccd1-47a6-8a57-a38660bab40d>>>'s exit vector, camera-right and slightly up. Heavy pieces travel flat parabolas, hit the roof, and slide. Fine lime dust hangs, then is shaped by the wing downwash. Tiles rattle in place from the structural jolt, and only the three that the wing tip levers actually come free.

Mass. <<<7ac036f0-ccd1-47a6-8a57-a38660bab40d>>> weighs 550 kg, and every contact shows it: the gable shudders on the first impact, the sill splits under its foot, the roof slates dip where it pushes off, and the roof jolt is what breaks <<<c48907ec-60b9-436a-b590-9e75b6b11588>>>'s footing. Its wingbeats are slow, about one per second, with visible loading and flex through the primaries and a heavy audible air displacement. It cannot hover: the first two beats convert into forward translation with the body sinking between strokes, and it only begins to climb after the third. Its neck extends and retracts like a real corvid's. The flight line out of frame is straight and committed, no banking, no circling.

Bodies. <<<c48907ec-60b9-436a-b590-9e75b6b11588>>> weighs 80 kg and the sword is heavy: the blade has inertia in the guard, accelerates through the cut and would carry him past his own centre if it met nothing — which is exactly what happens. In free fall he accelerates properly, 9.81 m/s², so the last third of the fall is covered in a fraction of the time of the first third. The coat has cloth delay behind his body, hair delay behind his head, and both stream upward against the fall. He never floats, never slows, never hangs.

PHYSICS
Materials completely real: skin, cloth, feathers, forged steel, slate, plaster, brick, glass, dust. The roof being flat is why friction and not slope governs his footing — driving strides on smooth dusty level slate with poor grip, slates shifting and dust bursting under each footfall, and the push-off is one loaded stride into a ballistic arc he cannot alter once his boots leave the roof. The sword has real mass on his back: it rides against his spine and its weight shifts with every stride, and the draw is one practiced motion over the right shoulder without breaking stride — the retaining loop flicks off the copper gear, the freed straps snap back against his coat and then flap loose for the rest of the clip. The window shatters as a slow expanding sheet; the wings open with the real inertia of a five-to-six-metre span and shove a wall of air ahead of them that snaps his coat and hair. The bird is already at full flight speed as it leaves the wall and simply sustains it — not a dodge, not an acceleration. The sword keeps that weight in the one hand that holds it at the end: it hangs and swings from his wrist under its own mass rather than being held aimed, and the copper gear at its base carries that same weight with it.

Cigar physics are exact. The arm carries real weight: the elbow bends and straightens with the mass of a forearm, the hand decelerates into position rather than snapping there, and the cigar is thick and firm, held between index and middle finger; the lips close on it without clamping. The stub-out is a crush against a hard flat plane, not an explosion. Because the surface is the flat front glass of the lens, nothing sinks in and everything the crush throws travels sideways along that plane, radiating out from the single point of contact. The ash cone is brittle and shatters into grey flakes and dust. The coal underneath is a fragile crust of burning tobacco: it flattens, then breaks into a dozen or so small irregular fragments that fly outward in short flat radiating arcs, tumbling as they go, cooling visibly from orange through dull red to grey and dying within about a third of a second. They do not streak, do not leave long light trails and do not shower. The wrapper folds and splits under the pressure, tobacco leaf frays out of the crushed end, and a thick slug of smoke is forced out of the body of the cigar all at once. What is left behind on the glass is a round black char mark about the width of the cigar, with fine ash streaks pulled radially out of it and a dull orange ring cooling around its edge.

Walking is real: heel contact, weight transfer through the foot, hip shift, toe push-off, the mass of a body arriving and stopping. He covers ground the way a man closing a distance does, not the way a figure slides forward.

His body is that of a man standing, not seated and not leaning: he holds his own height, the weight passes down through both feet, and the small balance corrections of standing run through his hips and shoulders. The T-shirt hangs in one clean vertical fall from his chest, moving only with his breath and with his steps. The dog tags shift and settle against his chest and swing slightly as he walks.

Smoke is thick and slow, not vapour: it leaves in soft columns that rise, fold over on themselves and tear apart where his breath crosses them. There is no wind: it behaves as smoke in still air, except where his own movement drags it as he walks in.

The chair transmits the impact through its post as one small damped shudder, barely perceptible, and is still again almost at once. Heavy monastic robes hang with real cloth weight and stay still. Damp cotton reads one to two shades darker than the dry khaki-olive around it, with soft irregular edges rather than clean shapes, and it picks up a faint low sheen only where the key rakes across it. The space behind him is unbroken dense black with no visible surface in it and no colour in it. FORMAT MODE
Single continuous take. No cuts, no dissolves, no fades, no transition effects. Real-time motion throughout.

OPTICS
ARRI Alexa Mini with vintage prime glass. 47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character with macro close focus, held constant for the whole shot. Every framing change comes from bodies moving in space: never a zoom, the field of view never changes, there is no zoom breathing. Camera distance goes from 0.2 m at the eye macro out to 2.6 m at the medium shot, then back to about 0.55 m as he walks at the lens, and the perspective on his face changes accordingly at every stage — macro exaggeration at the start, normal proportion in the middle, and a wide-angle looming closeness at the end with his brow and cap brim spreading toward the frame edges.

The retreat is not uniform. The operator's first backward steps are very small and each one after is a little longer, so the apparent rate of change stays even instead of racing at the start and crawling at the end. Distance milestones going out: about 0.20 m at 0.9s, 0.35 m at 2.5s, 0.65 m at 4.0s, 1.00 m at 5.5s, 1.45 m at 7.0s, 2.00 m at 8.5s, and 2.60 m when the move stops at 10.2s. Coming back in, the distance is his: about 2.60 m at 11.8s, 1.70 m at 12.4s, 1.05 m at 12.9s and 0.55 m at 13.4s.

The glass renders like old glass: slightly lower micro-contrast than modern lenses, gentle falloff toward the frame edges, a trace of field curvature so the corners sit softer than the centre, faint warm veiling flare lifting the deepest shadows a little, small amounts of coloured fringing on the hardest speculars, imperfect oval bokeh in the out-of-focus black and in the out-of-focus smoke. Faint optical halation appears only around the brightest speculars, the eye catchlights and, at the very end, the scattering embers; the skin itself never glows.

Focus is pulled by hand. It mostly holds his eyes, with the late corrections of a human focus puller: two or three visible settles across the shot. When he walks in, the puller falls behind and catches up twice, so he goes soft for a few frames each time before snapping back. At 0.55 m the depth of field is paper-thin: his eyes are sharp and his cap brim and hands are already soft.

CAMERA
Shoulder-mounted documentary handheld. The operator is on his own feet the whole time and the camera is never on a rig.

Every backward step registers in the frame: a small vertical dip as the weight lands, a lateral sway to the side of the standing leg, and a moment of near-stillness between steps, so the retreat is uneven, a little faster inside each step and almost stopped between them. The steps come slowly and grow longer as he goes, roughly one every one and a half seconds. On top of the steps sits the operator's slow breathing as a small vertical float, and the horizon rocks a degree or two either way without being levelled out.

The framing is careless rather than composed, but never loose enough to lose him. His head is not placed on any grid: it sits a little off-centre and a little low or high at different points, the frame drifts two to four percent and gets corrected a fraction of a second late, and some drifts are never corrected at all. Around 6.0s the drift runs a little further than elsewhere before being brought back, late and imprecisely. He stays broadly centred through the whole retreat and never slides toward a frame edge. No digital shake, no random jitter, no gimbal glide, no whip pan.

The descent at 9.2s is the operator's crouch, not a camera move and not a change in the subject: his knees bend and the whole frame sinks with the compression of a body lowering itself, about 45 centimetres over a second, with a small overshoot and settle as his weight arrives, and a matching slow tilt up so the standing man stays in frame.

When the man starts walking in, the operator holds his ground: he does not retreat and does not stand up. His only reaction is a small instinctive lean backwards that dips and tilts the frame a few centimetres, and a late upward tilt to keep the approaching face in shot as it grows. The framing gets worse, not better — his head crowds the top edge and the operator does not fully correct it.

When the man's hand closes over the front of the lens the frame lurches: it drops a few centimetres, rotates about five degrees, and then goes unnaturally still, held from the front by a hand that is not the operator's, with only the operator's breathing left in it. The operator does not let go, the camera never leaves his shoulder, it never falls, never spins and never points away from the man, and the frame never goes fully black.

PHYSICS
The eyelids have weight: they lift with the muscle behind them, the lashes separate and settle, the skin of the upper lids folds and unfolds instead of sliding. Both lids move on the same beat and at the same speed. The eyes are wet, with a real corneal specular rather than a painted dot, and the hard source puts one small sharp-edged catchlight in each eye. The pupils sit mid-dilated and stay stable.

Eye tracking is physically correct: the eyeballs rotate in their sockets to stay on the lens while the head barely moves, so the amount of visible white changes slightly from side to side as he follows the dipping, swaying, sinking frame, and each correction is a small quick saccade followed by a steady hold rather than a smooth glide.

Cigar physics are exact. The arm carries real weight: the elbow bends and straightens with the mass of a forearm, the hand decelerates into position rather than snapping there, and the cigar is thick and firm, held between index and middle finger; the lips close on it without clamping. For the whole first thirteen seconds its tip stays a long grey ash cone with a dull dark-red coal beneath, mostly hidden by the ash and unchanging in appearance, except that on a draw the cheeks hollow slightly, the coal deepens in colour for a moment and returns, and the ash cone grows longer, greying and beginning to crack at its tip. Ash never falls on its own.

The stub-out is a crush against a hard flat plane, not an explosion. Because the surface is the flat front glass of the lens, nothing sinks in and everything the crush throws travels sideways along that plane, radiating out from the single point of contact. The ash cone is brittle and shatters into grey flakes and dust. The coal underneath is a fragile crust of burning tobacco: it flattens, then breaks into a dozen or so small irregular fragments that fly outward in short flat radiating arcs, tumbling as they go, cooling visibly from orange through dull red to grey and dying within about a third of a second. They do not streak, do not leave long light trails and do not shower. The wrapper folds and splits under the pressure, tobacco leaf frays out of the crushed end, and a thick slug of smoke is forced out of the body of the cigar all at once. What is left behind on the glass is a round black char mark about the width of the cigar, with fine ash streaks pulled radially out of it and a dull orange ring cooling around its edge.

Walking is real: heel contact, weight transfer through the foot, hip shift, toe push-off, the mass of a body arriving and stopping. He covers ground the way a man closing a distance does, not the way a figure slides forward.

His body is that of a man standing, not seated and not leaning: he holds his own height, the weight passes down through both feet, and the small balance corrections of standing run through his hips and shoulders. It is a heavy body and it behaves like one: the balance corrections are slow and wide because there is a lot of mass riding on them, the breath moves the whole chest and the shoulders with it, and every movement starts from the trunk and arrives with weight rather than snapping. The T-shirt is stretched taut over the chest and shoulders and across the back, the sleeve hems gripping the upper arms, and below the chest it hangs in one clean vertical fall, moving only with his breath and with his steps; the damp patches move with the fabric and stay in the same places on it. The dog tags lie on a broad chest, shift and settle against it and swing slightly as he walks.

The veins are live tissue, not drawn lines: they sit raised under the skin with the skin stretched over them so they read by their own shadow and a soft highlight along the top rather than as dark strokes, they follow real anatomy — cephalic vein over the outside of the bicep, a branching network across the forearm, the back of the hand, one down the side of the neck, one at the temple — and they fill and flatten with what he does. They swell when the arm lifts and the hand closes, when he holds a breath on a draw, on the line, and on each step of the walk in; they settle back when the arm hangs. They never pulse rhythmically and never glow.

Speech is physical and quiet, and it happens only once: low breath support, minimal jaw travel, lips barely parting, no theatrical mouth shapes. For the rest of the shot his mouth is closed, holding the cigar, drawing or exhaling, and it never shapes words.

Smoke is thick and slow, not vapour: it leaves in soft columns that rise, fold over on themselves and tear apart where his breath crosses them. There is no wind: it behaves as smoke in still air, except where his own movement drags it as he walks in.

LIGHTING
One hard light source, just outside the frame, roughly 50 degrees to camera-left of where he stands and about 15 degrees above his eyes, fixed in place in the space for the whole shot, warm tungsten quality around 2800 to 3000 K, small enough to throw hard edges. It comes in low enough to pass under the brim of his cap: the brim throws a hard-edged shadow across his forehead above his eyebrows, and both of his eyes stay clear of it. This is the only light in the shot.

For the first eleven seconds, deep dramatic low key. A clear terminator runs down his face and continues down his body: the camera-left plane is lit and the camera-right plane goes down about four stops. The nose throws a hard shadow down and across the camera-right cheek, the brow shadow sits hard in the camera-right eye socket, and the light dies before it reaches his camera-right jaw. Speculars land only on the highest points of skin: the top of the cheekbone, the bridge of the nose, the sweat on his temple, the lower lip. The falloff continues downward but does not kill his chest: the light reaches far enough for the dinosaur-skeleton print to stay clearly legible about two stops under his face, its faded white lines picking up the key on the camera-left side and sinking into shadow on the camera-right side, and below the print the light dies out into black. One dog tag catches a hard bright edge. The same key rakes across the near shoulder, the deltoid and the upper arm and along the top of the forearm, so the mass reads by its own modelling and the raised veins catch a thin broken highlight along their tops with a fine shadow under them. Where the shirt is damp it reads a shade or two darker than the dry cotton with a faint low sheen only where the key crosses it, and the sweat on the temple, the neck cord, the collarbones and the tops of the shoulders and forearms breaks into small hard speculars. Deep as it is, this key never loses him while he is standing still: his lit plane, his eyes inside the brim shadow, his chest print and his arms all stay readable out to the medium shot, and the standing framing is never a silhouette. No fill, no bounce, no rim on the back of the head, no fixture in frame.

Because the source is fixed in the space, walking at the camera takes him out of its throw. Across those three steps the light on him rakes further and further round and falls away: the lit plane of his face narrows to a hard bright contour down the camera-left edge of his face, jaw and cap, his features sink into a dense warm shadow, and only the wet edges of his eyes keep catching the light. By 13.4s he is a hard-rimmed near-silhouette filling the frame, still readable in shape but almost gone in detail. Do not add any light to keep his face up; let it go.

The scattering fragments are the last light on him. For about a third of a second at 13.7s they throw a low, deep-orange bounce up onto the underside of his jaw, his cheekbones and the inside of both hands, hard and unstable, and it dies with them. After that the brightest thing left in the frame is the dull orange ring around the char mark itself, cooling toward black across the final second, with his hard contour just readable around it and everything else gone.

Colour is entirely warm: near-black, oxblood, maroon and burnt orange rust, with no cold tone anywhere in the frame. Highlights roll off gently and hold their texture rather than blowing out. Fine organic grain and low-level shadow noise, never scrubbed clean.

Maximum photographic realism. Real young skin with pores, a day of stubble, sun damage, dirt, sweat and asymmetry; the vertical scar above his left brow catching the light along its edge; the wet edge of the lower lid; individual lashes; veins raised under real stretched skin rather than painted on it; real worn cotton with a real print cracked by washing, taut where the body fills it and darkened where it is damp. It reads as recorded through old glass onto a real sensor, with no glow on the skin, no bloom, no halo, no glossy plastic surface, no beauty retouching, no sharpening edges.

AUDIO
He says two words and nothing else, at 10.4s: "Even now." Quiet, low, unhurried and menacing in its calm, with no raised volume, no growl and no whisper theatrics. It is said the way a man states a fact to someone who has just proved he does not deserve one — flat, faintly contemptuous, the second word dropped rather than pushed, and not a syllable of it spent trying to convince them. There are no words at all before 10.4s and none after it, and his lips are completely still for the entire first ten seconds. No narration, no offscreen voice, no music, no subtitles.

The line answers something that was asked before this shot began and is never heard here. Nothing from it is shown, and no other person or place appears in the frame.

Around the line: a near-silent low room tone with almost no high frequency. The faint dry crackle of the cigar on each draw. A slow sub-bass presence builds through the retreat and does not resolve. His slow breathing is audible in the long silence — a big man's breath, deep and unhurried, moving real volume. Three sets of unhurried footsteps as he closes the distance, close and dry, heavy enough that each one lands with weight. The dull knock and rasp of a hand closing on the camera body, then the short scrape and hiss of the cigar being crushed against it, and the small ticking of cooling fragments. No music at any point.

ACTING TASK — <<<image_4>>> (he is fully invested in his tactic; the work happens in his eyes)
EVENT: permission to look at him is revoked, and taken back by hand.
SCENE DIRECTION, shared and unspoken: keep it ordinary, and let nobody turn this into what it actually is.
PHYSICAL ACTION, the terrain: smoking, and taking his time about it, while they back away from him.
CONTRAST PAIR. HIM — sovereign (+) / contemptuous (−): the room is his, and he holds the people in it cheap. THEM, the operator and whoever sent him, unseen — curious (+) / hiding behind the glass (−): they want the thing itself and they want to watch it from a safe distance. ESSENTIAL AXIS: who is allowed to look at whom. On that axis he is plus and they are minus, and by the end he settles it physically.
MOTIVE, his fuel: he has stood in front of people like these before. They come, they ask, they get what they came for, and it never costs them anything; he is the one who paid for the thing they are pointing a lens at. That makes him their superior in the only currency that counts in this room, and he has no intention of pretending otherwise to make them comfortable.
GOAL: to make them drop their eyes first, and to leave them in no doubt about who they were standing in front of.
OBSTACLE: they do not drop them. They keep the camera up and keep backing away, and behind the glass they think they are not in the room — which lets them look at him for free. He cannot reach a person through equipment, and everything he gives turns into their footage. And he cannot be seen trying: the moment he pushes, they own the moment instead of him.
TACTIC: he holds their eye and waits for the flinch. He prices them — checking both of their eyes for the second one of them looks at the monitor instead of at him, and counting every backward step as ground they hand over. He makes them wait: each draw on the cigar is time spent in front of people who want something from him, and he spends it slowly to show that their waiting costs him nothing. He gives no help at all — no smile, no answer, no easing of the silence — and lets whatever they do with that be their own verdict on themselves. When the answer finally goes into them and they still keep filming for free, he stops negotiating with a lens and collects in person: he walks over, closes their eye with his hand, and puts the cigar out on it, so the looking ends on his terms and not on theirs.
Moment to moment:
— On the lid-lift: he does not wake up and then notice them. The eyes open already knowing someone is there and already deciding whether these ones are worth the trouble; the first thing he does is find their eyes, take them, and not give them back.
— Through the first stretch: he is pricing them, not waiting. He measures how close they dare stand and how long they will last, hunts both eyes for the flinch, and registers each retreating step as ground given up to him. If one of them glances down at the monitor instead of at him, he notes it and thinks less of them.
— The draw at 2.2s: taken instead of answering — making them wait, and making it plain that he can afford to and they cannot.
— The long look from 3.6s: he gives them nothing and watches what they do with nothing. Their discomfort in the silence is the most interesting thing in the room to him.
— The longer draw at 5.4s: he spends their time on purpose, unhurried, in front of a camera that is waiting on him.
— From 7.4s, the arm down: he stops occupying himself. Nothing is left between him and them but the look, and the look says he will outlast them.

The convulsion is an active flexor contraction against gravity — quick in, held and trembling, then released — and the release is passive, so the opening is slower than the closing and damped by the tissue itself, never elastic and never bouncing. Muscle tone leaves with the release, so the hand's final resting curl is slightly more open and slightly lower than its first — a limb that has stopped holding itself. Venous pooling darkens the fingertips and the nail beds slightly, the lowest part of the hand. The armrest pad is soft leatherette over foam and holds a visible compression dent under the forearm; that dent does not change, because the forearm never shifts its weight. The tunic keeps its folds. The cloth of <<<727185f3-d796-42dc-8472-4c373b08a49c>>> hangs plumb and stays exactly where it hangs; heavy wool at rest does not stir on its own. PHYSICS
Everything carries real weight. The pistol has real mass and its shot lands with real force. The bullet travels one straight line and pushes material outward on the camera side of the chair, never inward. Leather does not cut cleanly: it resists, stretches and then tears along its fibres, so the rip follows the weak lines of the hide and comes out crooked and uneven, with splits running further wherever the material was thinner or already creased. The torn petals stay stiff and hold whatever angle they were bent to. Foam threads pull out and hang, soot and powder settle on the surface around the entry, dust falls under gravity and settles. The chair transmits the impact through its post as one small damped shudder, barely perceptible, and is still again almost at once. Heavy monastic robes hang with real cloth weight and stay still. Bodies keep grounded mass and contact; no floating motion, no sliding feet, no teleporting between poses.
